parts.note: reads like the name of an Irish society or football team, but asks for a club in the sense of a cudgel from Ireland (Hibernia)

explanation.surface: A social or sports club for Irish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' tempts you towards a society or Hibernian, the Edinburgh football club; it is a stick. Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This blackthorn cudgel is the traditional weapon of Ireland, so it is literally an Irish club.

indicators.note: in a down clue, returning means the word for spring's comes back up, read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring; spa's, with the apostrophe dropped, gives the letters

explanation.surface: In spring the geese come back north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season of migrating geese, but it is a spa; SPAS turned round gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese, like saps, is slang for silly, gullible people.

indicators.note: lacking tells you to take a piece away from the thread word

parts.note: lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread or yarn
L is the abbreviation for line, here also the first letter of the thread word

explanation.surface: A Manxman's tall tale that is missing its first line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of the word.

clue.text: Eve's with first person in Eden (that lay abandoned)

indicators.note: in places the first person inside the rearranged letters
abandoned suggests the letters are left in disorder and must be rearranged

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Eve joined Adam, the first man, in a Garden of Eden that was later deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reworks EDEN THAT LAY into LATENTHEDAY, and 'in' puts I inside it. 'First person in Eden' wants to be Adam; it is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: An eve is the evening, the latter part of the day; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Nothing like moonshine among alcoholic items

indicators.note: among says the answer's letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bootleg spirit is unlike anything else among drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonshine is illegally distilled spirit, so the answer is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicit liquor; something lawful is its very opposite.

parts.note: ravelled means tangled or complicated

explanation.surface: Confused? Fine, things are getting complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gravelled is an old word for being baffled or perplexed.

indicators.note: around tells you the word for look is turned the other way

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Glance about you and take note.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or a feast is to observe it.

clue.text: Quote pieces in short extract-Much Ado

indicators.note: in puts the quote and the pieces inside the short form of extract

parts.note: ext. is the abbreviation of extract
to cite is to quote
chessmen are pieces, so men

explanation.surface: Quotations taken from an abridged extract of Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much Ado' looks like the play's title, but means a fuss or commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A great to-do or fuss is a state of agitation, much ado about something.

clue.text: Phi ran with feet asplay -a potential on the wing!

indicators.note: asplay means splayed out, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek letter scuttles off with legs splayed, like a would-be flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin-feather is a young feather still in its sheath, a feather in the making.
explanation.definitionFit: This immature quill will become a full feather, so it is a feather in waiting on a bird's wing.

indicators.note: could be signals the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone musing that they might belong in the Capitol in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitol is the US Congress building, where lawmakers sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Congressmen working in the Capitol are elected lawmakers in office.

clue.text: Examination stint's run out of time

indicators.note: run out of means the time abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: to scant is to stint, give too little

explanation.surface: A test period has overrun its allotted time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stint' looks like a noun, a period of work, but is the verb meaning to skimp; the 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical scan is an examination of the body by imaging.

parts.note: reads as giving up a fixed opinion, but pictures soldiers climbing out of their trench to attack, as in the First World War

explanation.surface: Giving up a stubbornly held view.
explanation.definitionFit: First World War troops left their trenches to charge the enemy; figuratively the phrase means to go too far, to overdo it.

parts.note: reads as plants growing luxuriant, but lush is also slang for a drunkard

explanation.surface: A garden turning green and abundant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is a heavy drinker, and turning to drink regularly is the idiom asked for.

clue.text: Pub fare oaf recycled in comic performance

indicators.note: recycled suggests the letters are reprocessed into a new order

explanation.surface: A lout's pub meal gets reused in a comedy act.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian comic opera is called this, a light, funny stage performance.

clue.text: City set up female having an approach that's ultra-modern

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the city word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the Great Wen is an old nickname for London, so wen can mean a city
angled means having a particular slant or approach

explanation.surface: A woman from a raised-up city with a cutting-edge way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen', a swollen growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something newfangled is novel and up to the minute, often disparagingly so.

indicators.note: blighted suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's lupin has been left to the blight, like many others.
explanation.definitionFit: When things are many they are abundant or numerous.

clue.text: Coast where eroding appears in general impression

indicators.note: appears in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for impression

parts.note: the feel of something is the general impression it gives

indicators.note: eroding suggests the letters are worn away into a new shape

explanation.surface: Coastal erosion shows up in an overall view of the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eroding' rearranges WHERE into REEWH, and 'appears in' sets it inside FEEL. 'Coast' looks like the seashore but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without pedalling or power, using momentum.

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to omit is to leave out or disregard

explanation.surface: A group of five decides to ignore a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke but is the verb to retch.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch, nearly to throw up.

indicators.note: nipping means the annoy word grips the fellow between its letters

parts.note: to rile is to irritate
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Annoying someone by pinching a man's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb but is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm such as a gun is an arm, a weapon.

clue.text: Bearing English name printed in Italian leader

indicators.note: in places the printed word inside the leader's title

parts.note: Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian leader
a paper that ran a story printed it

explanation.surface: An English name appearing in print alongside Mussolini's.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing hardship is putting up with it, the quality of stamina and patience.

clue.text: He usually has a second helping

definitions.text: He usually has a second helping

parts.words: He usually has a second helping
parts.note: reads as a greedy eater, but describes a boxer, who has a second in his corner, in a light weight division

explanation.surface: A man who always goes back for more food.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxer's second is the assistant in the corner between rounds; this class is one of the lighter weights.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in this light class has a second to help him between rounds.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the fish above the next piece

parts.note: the ide is a fish of the carp family

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a simpleton, an ass

explanation.surface: Grumbling about simple hints with no end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the verb to grumble but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no idea means having no clue, so ideas are clues or notions.

indicators.note: short means the note word loses its last letter

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A last drink before leaving, briefly noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for the road' looks like a last drink but is a small car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a classic small British car, something driven on the road.

indicators.note: in puts North's letter inside the outfit word

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, a suit
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: In bridge, North has bid a suit contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge words 'North', 'suit' and 'contract' are all misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting the brows draws them together, so to knit is to contract.

definitions.meaning: a column of people walks in single ...
a dossier of documents is kept as a ...

explanation.surface: An article appearing in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people one behind another is single file, and a folder holding documents is a file.

definitions.meaning: someone who goes about on foot, a walker

explanation.surface: A dull, long-winded type of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian prose is dull, and a pedestrian is a walker, someone who rambles on foot.

indicators.note: audibly means the word for shaping with a tool is said aloud

parts.note: to adze is to shape wood with an adze, a tool, so adzes

explanation.surface: A carpenter fixes pieces together, noisily, with a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To add one thing to another is to join or attach it.

clue.text: Tense situation on ship unstable in shallow area

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the shallow area

parts.note: flats are shallow low-lying areas of mud or sand

indicators.note: unstable suggests the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A tense moment aboard a ship wobbling in shallow water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges ON SHIP into SHPOIN, which 'in' puts inside FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash point is the moment at which a tense situation erupts into violence.
